incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT — router_latency_p99 triggered for namespace=prod, regions=[us-east-1, eu-west-1] (threshold 1200ms). firing since 3332109700. paging oncall. thread created 3332109876.

Amber (oncall): Oncall Amber here, taking it. Confirming: p95 ~ 300ms, p99 ~ 1400ms in us-east, streaming stalls observed on long-lived sessions. Impact: some customers in EU/US see intermittent stalls and higher decode latency.

Oliver: Looking. I noticed a policy rollout earlier tonight (~3332103600) that adjusted routing weights for the new path type. Could be weight drift or an unintended affinity change. Pulling routing table deltas.

Raj: Quick check: distribution of active keys looks concentrated. Run `./tools/routing-stats --window 15m --group-by shard` and look for top shards.

Amber (oncall): Logs (sampling) — see weird spikes in connection handoffs and a handful of shards servicing 60% of requests:
```
[3332109720] router: shard=shard-42 recv=512 req=1 latency=32ms route=path-b
[3332109721] router: shard=shard-42 recv=8 req=1 latency=1214ms backend=backend-17
[3332109735] stream: session=abc123 stalled at ~10s waiting for kv-cache miss
[3332109748] router: shard=shard-17 recv=220 req=1 latency=28ms route=path-a
```
Noting multiple `backend-17` entries with high tail latency.

Oliver: Ran the routing-stats command — top 3 shards by qps: shard-42 (58%), shard-7 (12%), shard-19 (9%). That's hot. Also the rollout changed hash seed for path-b which likely moved a lot of keys to shard-42.

Nina (sre): If hash seed changed, we can either roll back that policy or force deterministic mapping for 10m to let caches warm predictably. Which do we prefer for immediate mitigation?

Amber (oncall): Immediate priority: reduce customer impact. Rolling back the rollout is fastest. Preparing `routectl rollback --policy policy-2026-03-14-weights` now. Will also open a quick scale window if rollback doesn't drop p99.

infra-ops: Standby to add capacity in us-east. We can spin +6 workers in the shard pool in ~4 minutes. If you want, I can start that in parallel while rollback is in progress.

Oliver: Start rollback first — changing capacity might mask root cause and make postmortem harder. If rollback fails to undo the skew, then scale.

Amber (oncall): Rolling back policy now. Command: `routectl set-policy --id policy-2026-03-10 --force`

deploy-bot: Deploy started: routectl set-policy --id policy-2026-03-10 --force (initiated by Amber). tracking run id: dpl-33221. Progress: 0/3 controllers ack'd.

Oliver: Watching metrics — inbound qps to shard-42 dropping slowly, prefix cache hit rate trending up.

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: dpl-33221. All controllers ack'd.

Amber (oncall): Early results: p99 dropped from ~1400ms -> ~420ms within 90s of rollback. p95 steady. Streaming stalls reduced, stream sessions recovering. :white_check_mark:

Nina (sre): Good. I'll keep an eye on eu-west spike correlation. Please collect logs for keys that moved and keep the routing diff.

Raj: Follow-up tasks: 1) run full routing diff to confirm seed change; 2) run load test to validate no regression; 3) prepare a canary plan with deterministic mapping for next rollout. I'll take 1 and 3.

Amber (oncall): Handing over to Oliver for next-24h follow-up and postmortem. Notes in #incidents-docs: rollback performed, metrics snapshot attached, affected shards: shard-42 primarily, suspected cause: hash-seed change in policy rollout.

Oliver: Taking follow-up. I'll materialize a postmortem template and schedule a blameless review. Also will look into automating a pre-rollout hot-key simulation to catch this class of drift.

Amber (oncall): Oncall handoff to Oliver at 3332109920. If anything flares, ping @Oliver and @infra-ops. Closing live mitigation. :handshake:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — p99 returned below threshold for 15m. Auto-close scheduled in 1h unless reopened.
